A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same ETF research work. Text, figures, tables and appendices were readable and inspected, including Appendices A–C in v1 and A–E in v3.

before.justification: v1 reports original dataset annotation, hallucination-detection experiments in Table 2, summary analyses and NER evaluations in Appendix C.

after.justification: v3 retains these original empirical results and additionally reports hallucination-category proportions, preliminary Llama3-70B verification performance and a qualitative few-shot experiment outcome.

M1.justification: Section 5 retains code parsing, summary NER and filtering, entity matching, zero-shot intent verification and threshold-one summary aggregation. The added matching details explain the existing procedure; the unsuccessful few-shot trial does not replace the adopted method.

E1.justification: Both evaluate Java CodeXGLUE summaries from the same seven LLMs on entity-level and summary-level hallucination detection and NER. Table 1 retains 411 summaries and 9,933 entities. The category-distribution analysis adds no dataset, language or task coverage.

E2.justification: Section 6 newly reports evaluating Llama3-70B as an intent-verification alternative. In v1 it appeared among summary generators and NER models, without a reported intent-verification result. The Direct-versus-ETF comparator set in Table 2 and the Appendix C comparator sets remain unchanged.

E3.justification: Table 2 drops accuracy from the reported metric set. Section 5.2 adds a few-shot testing condition using example code and hallucinated summaries, while retaining zero-shot verification. Existing data counts and Appendix B settings remain unchanged; the PDFs do not establish that retained experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: New Figure 3 quantifies the distribution across the existing hallucination taxonomy. Section 5.2 adds a brief few-shot-versus-zero-shot finding without detailed ablation scores. The existing ungrounded-entity example and creative-summary and changed-entity-form error analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Both report Cohen's kappa of 0.72 for 4,354 doubly annotated tuples. Neither reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals or formal significance tests. The new category percentages are descriptive results, not uncertainty estimates.

E6.justification: v3 adds Llama3-70B intent-verification F1 of 0.37 and reports worse few-shot performance without scores. Figure 3 adds category shares: code complexity 52.9%, insufficient knowledge 29.7%, name bias 13.7% and natural-language context 3.8%. Table 2 removes six accuracy entries; its precision, recall and F1 values, including ETF's 0.73 F1, and Tables 1 and 3–5 remain unchanged.

T1.justification: Neither version supplies formal theorems or proofs. The hallucination definitions, taxonomy categories, working-memory motivation, threshold-one aggregation rule and NER metric descriptions retain their mathematical and conceptual substance.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list and conclusion retain the same central claims: a novel approximately 10K-entity dataset, a hallucination taxonomy and an interpretable ETF approach achieving 73% F1. The added diagnostics do not redefine these contributions.

C2.justification: Model selection is now explained through task complexity and poor preliminary open-model performance, replacing the confirmation-bias rationale. Section 9 adds parser-availability and large-model scalability limitations while removing prompt-sensitivity and explicit cross-language validation caveats. Section 5.2 newly attributes few-shot degradation to longer prompts.

D1.justification: Appendices D–E newly document matching rules, annotator qualifications, label guidance and taxonomy annotation. Section 3 explains random subsampling and annotation time, and Figure 5 corrects the description-field label. Conversely, Table 2 loses its macro-averaging specification. Hardware, generation settings and the planned code/data release remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v3 adds Valentin et al. (2024), Rebedea et al. (2023) and Mirzadeh et al. (2024), while removing Feng et al. (2024) and Xie et al. (2023). A new related-work paragraph emphasizes grounding against source code, and the added prompting discussion invokes reasoning limitations. The overall research positioning is retained.

P1.justification: Several paragraphs are shortened or rephrased across the introduction, related work, taxonomy, methodology and analysis. Annotation instructions are relocated and expanded in Appendix E, with Appendix D added for matching details. The main section order and overall narrative remain intact.

P2.justification: v3 adds the Figure 3 pie chart, revises Figure 2's title while retaining its taxonomy tree, and narrows Table 2 by removing accuracy. Example boxes and captions are adjusted, and appendix prompts are reordered and relocated. Figure 1 and the remaining table structures are substantially retained.

improvement.justification: Appendices D–E address specific documentation gaps in string matching and annotation, making the work easier to audit and reproduce. Figure 3 provides quantitative support for the taxonomy. These limited gains outweigh some reporting losses, including removal of accuracy, the macro-averaging specification and explicit cross-language validation caveats. The central experimental evidence and claimed performance remain unchanged.
